headline: US stocks trade mixed to lower as record SK Hynix listing tests AI-chip sentiment amid sector rotation and lingering Middle East risk
raw_text:
- SK Hynix (SKHYV) begins Nasdaq trading after raising $26.5 billion in the largest-ever US share sale by a foreign company, with ADRs priced at $149 under tickers SKHYV and SKHY
- Major US indices trade mixed to lower, with the Russell 2000 (IWM) underperforming and small caps lagging broader benchmarks
- Chip-related sentiment is mixed as investors weigh SK Hynix (SKHYV)’s AI and high-bandwidth memory exposure following recent semiconductor pullbacks
- Meta Platforms (META) shows pre-open strength while US chip stocks trade cautiously, even as AI-linked peers Hua Hong and SoftBank advance in Asia
- Filings for single-stock ETFs tied to the AI and semiconductor theme increase, underscoring continued product demand around the trade
- Delta Air Lines (DAL) falls roughly 2% despite beating earnings estimates, reinstating guidance, and signaling healthy travel demand, as investors focus on elevated fuel costs
- Sector flows indicate rotation out of some high-flying tech names and broader caution outside technology in a session with no major economic data catalysts
- Traders monitor SK Hynix (SKHYV)’s trading, next week’s bank earnings, and ongoing Middle East tensions, while major indices remain on track for a positive week
